limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).

Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking; a win the goldfish cannot see (`alt_win_cards`) multiplies speed's weight by 0.5.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.

DeckCheck's Threat Index is a component at prior weight 0.15 (2026-10-19): one LLM's dated read of card quality, withheld when it describes another list; its interval is a declared prior sd of 4.0 on the anchor until three decks carry two readings on one list; its score places within the bracket, its twelve rubric grades anchor.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.

The weights are a Dirichlet prior (κ = 20.0) and the inputs are drawn from their posteriors: `score` is the median of 2000 seeded draws, `score_ci` its 90% interval, and every sd in `uncertainty` is declared, not estimated.
A placement within a group of n is a (n−1)-point scale and earns the share λ = (n−1)/(n−1+4) of its component, the rest going to the cited anchor; at n=3 that is one third.
A divergent `concordance` — the deck's instruments rank it far apart — prints the grade as a range, never a letter, and the judgment must address every outlier instrument.
rank over n=5 decks; no significance claim

judgment.argument:
The components measure a list nobody has played yet. Every logged game predates this version, so the table record (0 wins in 5 games) describes older builds; pilot feel and Forge are withheld, and the Threat Index describes another list. That is the ground I fill in, and the record gives little.

Speed ranks the deck last. The deck has no two-card loop and ends by accumulation. The one verified kill, Bloodletter with Sanctum Seeker, is 4.4% assembled, but that is one declared route: Bloodletter doubles every opponent's loss on your turn, so I read any on-turn drain as pairing with it, a reading until a stack runs it. The converters are drawn in 61.8% of games. How long accumulation takes once one is drawn is unmeasured, so speed's reading stands as is.

Construction ranks first, mana third and resilience worse. Construction is the heaviest downward lever: leaving it out drops the composite by about five points, though the table record pulls the other way. The record does not explain any of the three. It holds no played game on this list, no cited fact that says construction's strength, mana's or resilience's weakness is real at a table.

So I sit at the measured score. The record gives no unmeasured fact that moves it either way, and the strategy's bracket three reading (strong synergy and one-big-turn kills off accrued resources, at least six turns) fits a late finisher without proving this one.
